items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: someone told me, I think Sid Catlett or someone told me that Fletcher was having auditions for guitar player.

ctx.x: Yeah, he said, but I'm over age. But any way, I never was -- I never tried to play like Charlie, still don't. But now, I told you that I was with Fletcher Henderson. I went to New York -- after my mother died I went to New York to live, 1938, '39, some time ago, '40. 1940. I had been to New York previously with Roy Eldridge. And this is really when I met Dizzy, was in 1937, at the Savoy Ballroom, when I was there with Roy Eldridge. But I went back in 1940 to live, and someone told me, I think Sid Catlett or…

didn't you tell me? But I had to get the job this way. Now, we'll go back again. I told you that I went to New York for the first time with Roy Eldridge. I worked with Roy. When he left Fletcher he formed a band, this was in '36. And I worked with Roy, I was in his band in Chicago, the Three Deuces. We had a tremendous band. But before that I had worked at the Three Deuces at Tatum for about two years. Now, this was --
